findings.detail: You are off both pedals here. Either brake later and trail the brake to the apex, or get back on the throttle sooner. Coasting is pure lost time.

findings.detail: You are off both pedals here. Either brake later and trail the brake to the apex, or get back on the throttle sooner. Coasting is pure lost time.

findings.title: T2: ABS active 43% of the braking
findings.detail: You are braking past the limit and letting ABS manage it. Ease off slightly once ABS starts, especially as you start turning in.

findings.title: T4: ABS active 67% of the braking
findings.detail: You are braking past the limit and letting ABS manage it. Ease off slightly once ABS starts, especially as you start turning in.

findings.title: T6: usually 1.4 m wider at the apex than your best lap
findings.detail: Turning in too early or carrying too much speed pushes you away from the apex. Turn in a little later and aim to clip the inside kerb.

findings.title: T4: brake released abruptly while turning
findings.detail: Snapping off the brake while turning unloads the front tyres and causes entry understeer. Trail off the brake gradually toward the apex.

findings.title: T1: throttle lifted again after picking it up
findings.detail: Picking up the throttle and then lifting usually means you got on it too early or too hard. Squeeze it on smoothly once, and only add more.

findings.title: T4: 2 steering corrections per pass
findings.detail: You keep re-adjusting the wheel mid-corner, which usually means the car is sliding or you turned in at the wrong point. Aim for one smooth input in and one smooth unwind out.

findings.title: T6: throttle lifted again after picking it up
findings.detail: Picking up the throttle and then lifting usually means you got on it too early or too hard. Squeeze it on smoothly once, and only add more.

setup.title: No consistent balance problem detected
setup.detail: Handling looks reasonably neutral from the data. Focus on driving technique first.

setup.title: RL: inside only 0.4°C hotter than outside
setup.detail: Not enough negative camber; the outside edge is working too hard. Add about 0.2-0.3° negative camber.

setup.title: RR: inside only -2.3°C hotter than outside
setup.detail: Not enough negative camber; the outside edge is working too hard. Add about 0.2-0.3° negative camber.

setup.title: Fronts running 16.5°C hotter

pros.title: Clean, repeatable lines through T2, T5
pros.detail: You hit the same apex as your best lap with no mid-corner corrections. That consistency is what lets you push braking points later.

pros.title: You commit to the brake pedal in 3 of 6 braking zones
pros.detail: You hit 90-100% brake pressure in T1, T5, T6. Many newer drivers never press hard enough; you do, and that's the foundation of late braking.

pros.title: Fast, decisive brake application (T2, T3, T4, T5)
pros.detail: You reach peak pressure in under 0.2 s. That is exactly right: the first part of the braking zone is where the tyres have the most grip.

pros.title: You get back on the throttle at the slowest point in 6 corners
pros.detail: Picking up the throttle at the apex (not after it) is good timing. The problem is what happens just before that point; see weaknesses.

pros.title: 56.5% of the lap at full throttle
pros.detail: Strong commitment on the straights and exits for this track.

cons.title: Coasting: 19% of the lap with neither pedal pressed
cons.detail: About 149 m per lap in T1, T2, T4, T5, T6. You come off the brake, roll, and only then pick up the throttle. The car is slowing with nothing controlling its balance, so you lose time and the front goes light before the apex.

cons.title: Braking into ABS in 2 corners
cons.detail: In T2, T4 ABS is active for 67% of the zone at worst. ABS is a safety net; leaning on it lengthens your stops and hides where the real limit is.

cons.title: Throttle on-off-on at the apex (T1, T6)
cons.detail: You pick up the throttle, lift, then reapply. That unsettles the car and usually means you went to the throttle too hard or too early.

cons.title: Brake released abruptly while turning (T4)
cons.detail: Snapping off the brake mid-turn-in unloads the front tyres and causes understeer at the apex.

cons.title: Running wide of the apex (T6)
cons.detail: T6: 1.4 m wider than your best lap. Missing the apex makes the corner longer and slower.

cons.title: Busy hands: steering corrections mid-corner (T4)
cons.detail: Repeated small corrections mean the car is moving around under you or the line needs adjusting mid-corner. Both cost speed.

cons.title: Inconsistent through T5, T3, T2, T1, T6
cons.detail: T5: 0.55 s between your average and best pass; T3: 0.38 s between your average and best pass; T2: 0.32 s between your average and best pass; T1: 0.25 s between your average and best pass; T6: 0.19 s between your average and best pass.

improve.title: Connect the brake to the throttle
improve.target: Coasting under 8% of the lap, and under 10 m in any corner
improve.how: Keep 10-20% brake on as you turn in and hold it until the slowest point, then go straight to a light throttle. No gap between the pedals. Practice only this for 5 laps, starting with T1, T2.

improve.title: Threshold braking: hard first, then bleed off
improve.target: ABS active less than 20% of each braking zone
improve.how: Hit the brake hard first, and the moment ABS starts working, ease off 5-10% instead of holding the pedal down.

improve.title: Hit the apex
improve.target: Within 0.5 m of your best line at every apex
improve.how: In T6, turn in slightly later and aim the car at the inside kerb. If you still can't reach it, you're carrying too much speed in: brake a touch more.

improve.title: Pick fixed reference points
improve.how: For T5, T3, T2: choose one brake marker (a board, a shadow, a kerb start) and one turn-in point, and use them every lap. Move the brake marker 5 m later only when you hit the apex 3 laps in a row.

stopDoing.title: Letting go of both pedals between braking and the apex
stopDoing.detail: Every metre without a pedal is time you are not using.

stopDoing.title: Holding the brake pedal flat and letting ABS do the work
stopDoing.detail: Ease off as soon as you feel ABS chatter or see the ABS light.

stopDoing.title: Stabbing the throttle and lifting again
stopDoing.detail: Pick it up once, gently, and only ever add more.

stopDoing.title: Snapping off the brake with the wheel turned
stopDoing.detail: Release it gradually over the last 20-30 m before the apex.

stopDoing.title: Sawing at the wheel
stopDoing.detail: One smooth turn in, hold, one smooth unwind. If you need to correct, the input before it was too sudden or too early.

show.item: Live delta to your best lap
show.why: The single most useful number. It turns green/red within a corner, so you instantly know whether a change you just tried worked.
Keep these on while you fix coasting (19% now): you'll see the gap between the red and green bars. Remove once it's under 8%.
Your ES wheel already has RPM LEDs, so you don't need to look at the HUD for shifts. Keep the gear number visible.

show.item: Last lap and best lap times
show.why: Glance on the main straight only.
Check after a few laps to see if you are overheating one end.

hide.item: Full standings / timing tower in practice
hide.why: Irrelevant when you are learning. Use the relative (gap to cars around you) only in races.
Useful for your first laps on a new track. After that, learn the track by real reference points instead.
Never read numbers in a corner. Look through the corner to the apex and exit; read the HUD only on straights.
Only matter in long races. Hide them in practice to reduce clutter.
